unprivileged_old_version_update.why: All v1-v4 price-mutating functions either require OracleAdminCap/OracleFeederCap (owned solely by 0x39c70d4c...) and/or are blocked by the per-version gate: live PriceOracle.version=4 != v1/v2 (==1), v3 (==2), v4 (==3). Old-version calls abort (incorrect_version). The same applies to OracleConfig (v3/v4 config gates expect 2/3, live=4). Residual: the single OracleAdminCap holder could call v1/v2 version_migrate to downgrade PriceOracle.version to 1 and then use old-version functions — admin-only, not unprivileged.

reward_checkpoint_bug.description: Deprecated v1/v2 claim paths treat a missing per-user reward checkpoint (index_rewards_paids / user_index) as index 0, so an account that was never settled appears to have earned the pool's full historical index x its current balance and can claim rewards for a window in which it held no balance.
reward_checkpoint_bug.deployed_bytecode_confirmed: main v26 and lineage C v21 incentive_v2::calculate_one is byte-identical (both 51407 bytes): LdU256(0) default for index_rewards_paid; reward_increase = (index_reward - index_rewards_paid) * user_balance
reward_checkpoint_bug.gate_status: claim path calls version_verification(incentive) via base_claim_reward/update_reward; live object versions match current constants (main 16/16, staging 15/15) so the CURRENT-version claim path is callable by anyone; old versions remain gated off.

reward_checkpoint_bug.impact_main_deployment: None at present: V2 pool_objs empty (no active pools) and all 9 V2 IncentiveFundsPool balances = 0; V1 has no funds pools at all.
reward_checkpoint_bug.impact_lineage_c_staging: Reachable: 8 active V2 pools reference non-empty funds (NAVX 0x015a4aa9 balance 203,626,432 raw; CERT 0x1ca8aff8 balance 50,111,179,527 raw). A user with a supply/borrow balance and no checkpoint can claim index_reward x balance / RAY capped by remaining pool supply and fund balance. WETH funds (98.4 WETH x2) are referenced only by inactive pools and are NOT reachable through this claim path (get_pool_from_funds_pool scans pool_objs only).

incidents.what: Volo Protocol vaults (WBTC, XAUm, USDC) drained ~$3.5M via compromised operator private key (social engineering), not a contract bug; Volo is a NAVI-group product that routes deposits into NAVI lending; NAVI stated no impact to NAVI user funds. DefiLlama lists it as NAVI's 1 recorded incident.

conclusions.oracle: Version-gated (live version 4); all price mutation in v1-v4 aborts on the live object; v1-v5 direct updates require OracleAdminCap/OracleFeederCap, all held by 0x39c70d4c...; current v5 additionally exposes a permissionless keeper path (oracle_pro::update_single_price_v2/v3) that accepts only signed source data with strategy checks. No unprivileged old-version oracle update path.
conclusions.lineage_c: NAVI staging/development lending_core deployment (original 0xa49c5d1c..., 21 versions, current 0xc371fc61...), controlled by 0xdf6bff0f...; version-gated (constants 6->15, live objects 15); old versions abort on gated functions. Non-empty V2 funds + active V2 pools make the (unmerged-fix) reward-checkpoint bug economically reachable here; main deployment is not affected (no active V2 pools, empty funds).
conclusions.additional_lineages_found: Only the main lending lineage (26 versions), oracle lineage (5 versions), lineage C staging (21 versions), the immutable uiGetter package, and type-origin packages for incentive_v2 (v9) / incentive_v3 (v22) / flash_loan (v14) within the main lineage. No other independent package origins were found among the SDK-listed objects.
